name: Gesture-Controlled Robot
description: Control a robot car with hand tilt using an accelerometer glove that sends commands wirelessly.
guide:
What you will build

A glove with an MPU6050 or ADXL335 sensor that tilts forward/back/left/right to drive a robot remotely.

What you will learn

  • How accelerometers detect tilt
  • How wireless modules pass sensor data between boards

Safety first

  • Test robot on blocks before floor drive
  • Keep batteries disconnected when wiring

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Wire accelerometer to transmitter Arduino
    Read x/y tilt values in Serial Monitor while moving glove.
  2. Pair nRF24L01 or HC-05 link
    Send tilt bytes from glove to robot receiver.
  3. Map tilt to motors
    Forward if y > threshold, back if y < -threshold, turn on x axis.
  4. Mount sensor on glove finger
    Secure board; strain-relief wires at wrist.
  5. Calibrate neutral
    Read flat-hand values; subtract offset in code.
  6. Drive test
    Slow PWM first. Partner wears glove, operator spots robot.

codes.title: Tilt to motor mapping

name: LEGO Spike Conveyor Belt System
description: Build an automated conveyor with LEGO Spike Prime that sorts objects by color into different bins.
guide:
What you will build

A moving belt that carries coloured blocks past a color sensor; a motor diverts each block to the correct bin.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build conveyor frame
    Follow Spike build instructions for belt and motor drive.
  2. Mount color sensor over belt
    Fixed height 5 mm above blocks.
  3. Program color detection
    When red detected → activate diverter motor one direction; blue → opposite.
  4. Test with 10 blocks
    Count sorting accuracy. Adjust sensor threshold in app.
  5. Add stop button
    Emergency stop stops all motors.
  6. Present flowchart
    Draw sense → decide → act loop.

name: LEGO Spike Robotic Crane
description: Build and program a LEGO Spike crane that lifts objects using precise arm and hook movements.
guide:
What you will build

A rotating crane with winch that picks up a load and places it in a marked zone without dropping.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Assemble crane base and rotating arm
    Test manual rotation smoothness.
  2. Add winch motor and hook
    String length limits max height.
  3. Program pick sequence
    Rotate to load → lower hook → raise 5 cm → rotate to drop zone → lower.
  4. Use force sensor (optional)
    Stop winch when tension detected.
  5. Accuracy test
    5 successful pick-and-place runs in a row.

name: LEGO Spike Dancing Robot
description: Build a humanoid LEGO Spike robot and program a dance routine synchronized to music.
guide:
What you will build

A biped or character robot that moves arms and legs in sequence to a 30-second music clip.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build stable humanoid
    Wide feet prevent tipping during arm swings.
  2. Plan 6 dance moves
    Sketch poses: arms up, twist left, twist right, bow, etc.
  3. Program each move with wait blocks
    Match beats — ~0.5 s per move for fast song.
  4. Add music block or play from tablet
    Start music and dance together on green button.
  5. Perform for class
    Record video; note one improvement for timing.

name: LEGO Spike Drawing Robot
description: Build a robot that holds a marker and draws geometric patterns on large paper.
guide:
What you will build

A cart robot with pen holder that draws a square and triangle by combining forward motion and turns.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build pen holder
    Marker tip pressed lightly — not too hard on paper.
  2. Tape paper to desk
    Mark robot start corner.
  3. Program square
    Repeat 4: move 20 cm, turn 90°.
  4. Calibrate distance
    Measure wheel circumference; adjust motor degrees.
  5. Add triangle routine
    Turn 120° between sides. Run second program.
  6. Display artwork
    Label dimensions measured with ruler.

name: LEGO Spike Racing Car Challenge
description: Design the fastest LEGO Spike racing car and time trials on a straight track.
guide:
What you will build

A lightweight Spike race car — you iterate wheel size and gear ratio for best 5-metre time.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build baseline car
    Two driven wheels, low profile.
  2. Mark 5 m track
    Masking tape start/finish.
  3. Time three runs
    Average time with stopwatch.
  4. Change one variable
    Larger rear wheels OR higher motor power setting.
  5. Retest and compare
    Table: design version vs average time.
  6. Class race
    Fair start — hand release on go signal.

name: LEGO Spike Catapult Launcher
description: Build a LEGO Spike catapult, program launch power, and measure projectile distance.
guide:
What you will build

A catapult that launches a ball when you press a button, with motor tension controlling distance.

Safety first

  • Launch only toward open area — never at people
  • Use soft projectiles only

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build catapult arm and latch
    Rubber band or motor tension stores energy.
  2. Program wind-up and release
    Motor pulls arm back 90°, releases quickly.
  3. Measure three distances
    Try low/medium/high power settings.
  4. Graph power vs distance
    Bar chart in notebook.
  5. Explain energy transfer
    Motor → elastic → kinetic of ball.

name: Soccer-Playing Robot
description: Build a robot that pushes a ball toward a goal in a mini robot soccer match.
guide:
What you will build

A low, wide robot with a front kicker plate that chases a ball and scores in a 60 cm goal.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Wide chassis and strong motors
    Low centre of mass resists tipping.
  2. Front kicker servo or fixed wedge
    Pushes ball without trapping underneath.
  3. Optional line sensor
    Stay in field boundary marked with tape.
  4. Drive practice
    Manual Bluetooth control first, then auto chase brightest ball (optional).
  5. Play 3-minute match
    Record goals. Discuss strategy: defend vs attack.

equipment.name: Tennis ball or robot soccer ball

// turn toward ball when off-centre

name: Stair-Climbing Robot
description: Design a robot with tracks or large wheels that climbs a model staircase or ramp.
guide:
What you will build

A high-torque tracked or tri-wheel robot that climbs foam stairs at least 3 steps without flipping backward.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build foam or wood mock stairs
    Step height 5 cm, depth 15 cm, 3 steps.
  2. Use tank tracks or oversized wheels
    Centre of mass forward of rear axle helps climb.
  3. High-torque geared motors
    Slow speed acceptable — torque matters more.
  4. Test approach angle
    Hit bottom step square-on; add front skid if needed.
  5. Iterate weight distribution
    Move battery forward if wheelies backward.
  6. Document failed attempts
    Photos + notes before final design works.

name: Color-Sorting Robot
description: Build a robot that detects block colours and sorts them into separate bins automatically.
guide:
What you will build

A conveyor or arm system with TCS3200 colour sensor that drops red blocks in bin A and blue in bin B.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Wire TCS3200
    Calibrate white balance on white paper first.
  2. Read RGB or frequency
    Print values for red vs blue blocks in Serial.
  3. Build chute with servo gate
    Left position = bin A, right = bin B.
  4. Place block on sensor platform
    Pause 1 s, classify, move gate.
  5. Sort 20 mixed blocks
    Count errors; tune thresholds.

codes.title: Color classify
codes.code:
// read red and blue channel values
// if(red > blue + margin) binA(); else binB();

name: Path-Driving Robot
description: Program a robot to follow a fixed path using timed moves and turns without line sensors.
guide:
What you will build

A robot that executes a stored sequence: forward 2 s, turn 90°, forward 1 s — drawing a square path on the floor.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Measure wheel travel
    Mark distance in 1 s at PWM 150.
  2. Measure turn accuracy
    Time or degree-based 90° pivot on spot.
  3. Write path array
    struct move {char type; int value;} path[] = ...
  4. Execute sequence on green button
    Robot returns near start after square.
  5. Reduce error
    Adjust turn delay 5 ms at a time.
  6. Draw planned path on paper
    Compare to tape outline on floor.

codes.title: Path sequence
codes.code:
void forwardMs(int ms) { /* both motors */ delay(ms); stop(); }
void turnRightMs(int ms) { /* left fwd, right back */ delay(ms); stop(); }
codes.description: Chain moves in loop or array.

name: Human Movement Walking Robot
description: Build a simple two-leg walking robot from cardboard and motors to study human-like gait.
guide:
What you will build

A biped frame where alternating leg motors lift and slide forward — slow walking motion on desk.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut cardboard legs and body
    Hip joints from bottle caps as pivots.
  2. One motor per leg
    Cam wheel lifts leg when rotated.
  3. Alternate legs in code or switch circuit
    Left up while right down, then swap.
  4. Support with hand for first tests
    Prevent fall until rhythm stable.
  5. Compare to human walk diagram
    Label stance and swing phases.

name: Alarm System with Bluetooth Alerts
description: Build a room alarm with ultrasonic detection that buzzes and sends alert text to a phone via Bluetooth serial.
guide:
What you will build

Ultrasonic sensor detects intruder within 1 m; buzzer sounds and HC-05 sends "ALERT" to phone Bluetooth terminal app.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Wire HC-SR04 and buzzer
    Same as parking sensor distance code.
  2. Pair HC-05 to phone
    Open serial terminal app at 9600 baud.
  3. On intrusion
    if(distance < 100) { buzzer; BT.println("ALERT"); }
  4. Add arm/disarm button
    Hold button 2 s to enable system.
  5. Test walk-through
    Phone receives message within 2 s.

codes.title: Bluetooth alert

name: Remote-Controlled Car
description: Assemble an RC car kit and practice throttle, steering, and safe driving on a marked course.
guide:
What you will build

A ready-to-run or kit RC car you learn to control through a slalom course of cones.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Charge battery fully
    Follow kit safety sheet for LiPo or NiMH.
  2. Bind transmitter to receiver
    Confirm steering trim centred.
  3. Learn controls
    Throttle trigger, steering wheel, reverse.
  4. Build cone course
    5 cones 1 m apart slalom.
  5. Time three laps
    Improve without knocking cones.
  6. Explain radio link
    Draw transmitter → receiver → motor diagram.

name: RC Airplane Assembly and Flight
description: Assemble a foam RC airplane kit, learn transmitter controls, and complete a supervised test flight.
guide:
What you will build

A foam electric RC plane with aileron, elevator, rudder, and throttle — flown only with certified instructor.

Safety first

  • Fly only at approved field with instructor
  • Check propeller area clear before arming
  • Pre-flight battery and control check every time

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Assemble fuselage and wings per kit
    Verify control surfaces move correct direction on transmitter.
  2. Centre of gravity check
    Balance on fingers at marked point on wing.
  3. Range check on ground
    Walk 30 m — controls still respond.
  4. Hand launch or runway takeoff
    Gentle throttle; climb straight.
  5. Practice turns at safe altitude
    Wide gentle banks.
  6. Log flight time
    Notebook entry: weather, battery, manoeuvres.

name: Quadcopter Building Kit
description: Assemble a quadcopter kit, calibrate the flight controller, and learn hover basics under supervision.
guide:
What you will build

A four-motor drone from a education kit with prop guards, configured in Betaflight or manufacturer app.

Safety first

  • Instructor required for first flights
  • Remove props when testing motors on bench
  • Follow local drone regulations

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Frame and motor assembly
    Motors diagonal pairs spin opposite directions.
  2. Solder ESCs and connect FC
    Teacher supervises soldering.
  3. Install propellers matched to motor spin
    Colour codes in manual.
  4. Calibrate accelerometer on level surface
    FC config software.
  5. Tethered hover test
    Light tether prevents flyaway.
  6. Log PID tuning notes
    What changed after first stable hover.

name: Wind Tunnel Construction
description: Build a small wind tunnel with a fan and test how different shapes experience lift and drag.
guide:
What you will build

A desktop wind tunnel: fan blows through a straight section where foam airfoils are mounted on a balance skewer.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build cardboard or acrylic duct
    Fan at one end, test section 30 cm long, exhaust wider.
  2. Mount test airfoil on rod
    Pivot shows pitch angle change.
  3. Observe thread tufts or smoke (teacher)
    See laminar vs turbulent flow.
  4. Compare flat plate vs curved airfoil
    Which lifts at 15° angle of attack?
  5. Measure deflection on simple balance
    Relative lift comparison only.
  6. Write lab report
    Diagram + three observations.

name: Helicopter Spinner Design
description: Design paper helicopters with different blade shapes and measure spin rate and fall time.
guide:
What you will build

Three paper helicopter designs dropped from 3 m — you time descent and count rotations.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut template T-shape
    Fold blades opposite directions for spin.
  2. Design B: wider blades
    Design C: add paper clip weight on stem.
  3. Drop from approved height
    Teacher supervises balcony or ladder.
  4. Count spins with slow-motion phone video
    Or partner counts aloud.
  5. Table results
    Design vs fall time vs spin count.

name: Bottle Rocket with Fins
description: Design bottle rocket fins for stable flight and test how fin size affects altitude.
guide:
What you will build

Water rocket with three or four cardboard fins — compare small fins vs large fins in flight stability.

Safety first

  • Outdoor launch with goggles
  • Teacher operates pump above 40 psi max

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build nose cone and fin sets
    Two bottles: fin set A small, set B large.
  2. Align fins symmetrically
    120° apart for three fins.
  3. Launch at 30 psi
    Observe wobble vs straight flight.
  4. Record apex and stability rating 1–5
    Three launches each design.
  5. Conclusion on fin area
    Link to arrow stability in physics.

name: Airfoil Testing and Comparison
description: Cut foam airfoils of different shapes and compare lift using a fan and simple balance.
guide:
What you will build

Three foam wing profiles tested in front of a fan — measure upward force on a kitchen scale or spring scale.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut symmetric, cambered, and flat plates
    Same chord length 15 cm.
  2. Mount on stand at 10° angle
    Into the fan airflow.
  3. Record scale reading
    Higher grams = more lift (relative).
  4. Repeat at 0° and 20°
    Table angle vs lift per shape.
  5. Explain camber
    Why curved upper surface helps.

name: Flying Ring Hoop Glider
description: Build a ring-wing hoop glider from paper or foam strips and test its unusual stable flight.
guide:
What you will build

A circular wing glider made from a light foam or paper loop that glides slowly when thrown gently.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Form loop 20 cm diameter
    Tape strip ends; add small straw fuselage through centre.
  2. Throw level with moderate speed
    Too hard causes stall.
  3. Try wider and narrower loops
    Compare glide distance.
  4. Draw cross-section sketch
    Label loop wing and centre body.

name: Boomerang Construction
description: Design and throw cardboard boomerangs, observing curved flight and return path.
guide:
What you will build

A 3-arm or V-shape boomerang from cardboard — test if it returns or curves predictably.

Safety first

  • Throw in open field away from people
  • Wait for return before next throw

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Trace template on thick cardboard
    Each arm 25 cm, slight airfoil bevel on leading edge.
  2. Curve wings slightly upward
    Like aeroplane wing dihedral.
  3. Throw vertical spin
    20° upward, snap wrist for rotation.
  4. Video flight path
    Sketch path — does it return?
  5. Modify one arm length
    Retest; note behaviour change.

name: Wingsuit Design Challenge
description: Build a wingsuit for an action figure and test glide ratio from a safe drop height.
guide:
What you will build

Fabric or paper wings on a toy figure that slows descent when dropped from 3 m.

Safety first

  • Drop only over foam pad
  • Teacher approves drop point

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Measure baseline drop time without wings
    Same figure, same height.
  2. Attach wings with arms spread
    Surface area maximised.
  3. Measure glide time and horizontal drift
    Glide ratio = horizontal / vertical drop.
  4. Iterate wing area
    Larger wings should slow fall.
  5. Relate to real wingsuits
    One paragraph on human flight sports.

name: Scratch Pong Game
description: Recreate classic Pong with two paddles, bouncing ball, and score tracking in Scratch.
guide:
What you will build

Two-player Pong: left paddle W/S, right paddle up/down arrows, ball bounces with score on sides.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Create ball sprite
    Move continuously; bounce on edge.
  2. Paddle sprites at sides
    Constrain y movement to stay on screen.
  3. Ball bounce on paddle
    if touching paddle, reverse x direction and add slight y from paddle position.
  4. Score variables
    Left score when ball hits right edge past paddle.
  5. Win at 5 points
    Display winner message.

name: Scratch Maze Game
description: Create a maze navigation game with timer, moving obstacles, and treasure collection.
guide:
What you will build

Player navigates maze backdrop avoiding patrolling enemy sprite to reach treasure before time runs out.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Draw maze backdrop
    Black walls, player cannot pass wall colour.
  2. Arrow key movement
    if not touching wall colour, move 4 steps.
  3. Enemy patrol script
    forever: move and bounce on walls.
  4. Timer countdown from 60
    Game over if time hits 0.
  5. Treasure win
    touching treasure → next level backdrop.

name: Scratch Racing Game
description: Build a top-down racing game with track, lap timing, and checkpoint gates.
guide:
What you will build

Car sprite follows track; crossing checkpoint line increments lap; best lap time displayed.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Import or draw track backdrop
    Define road colour for stay-on-road optional penalty.
  2. Car rotates with left/right keys
    Up key moves in direction car points.
  3. Checkpoint line sprite
    broadcast lap complete; increment lap variable.
  4. Lap timer
    Reset on each lap; store best time.
  5. Three-lap race mode
    Display total time at finish.

name: Scratch Educational Quiz
description: Build an interactive subject quiz in Scratch with multiple choice, score, and certificate screen.
guide:
What you will build

Five-question science quiz with clickable answer buttons, score variable, and celebratory backdrop at 80%+.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. List questions in notebook
    Four options each, one correct.
  2. Question backdrop per stage
    Or one sprite shows question text.
  3. Button sprites A B C D
    broadcast answerChosen with letter.
  4. Check answer
    change score by 1 if correct; next question.
  5. Final score screen
    if score >= 4 show certificate backdrop.

name: Scratch Music Composer
description: Create an interactive music maker in Scratch with instrument buttons and recorded playback.
guide:
What you will build

On-screen piano keys (sprites) that play notes; record sequence and play back loop.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Create 8 key sprites
    Each plays different drum or note when clicked.
  2. List variable recording
    Append note number on each key press.
  3. Play button
    foreach note in list: play and wait 0.3 s.
  4. Clear recording button
    delete all of list.
  5. Compose 8-note melody
    Perform for class.

name: AI Chatbot Creation
description: Extend a Python chatbot with keyword matching and optional simple pattern library for STEM FAQs.
guide:
What you will build

A chatbot that matches user words to a dictionary of topics (photosynthesis, gravity, fractions) and returns stored answers.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Start from rule-based bot
    Dictionary mapping keywords to responses.
  2. Add fuzzy matching
    if any keyword in user message: respond.
  3. Load Q&A from JSON file
    Easier to add topics without code changes.
  4. Handle unknown gracefully
    Suggest topics list.
  5. Optional: use free API
    Teacher-approved only; discuss privacy.
  6. Test 15 questions
    Log success rate.

Code to upload

Keyword chatbot (Python)

import json
answers = json.load(open('faq.json'))
while True:
    msg = input('You: ').lower()
    if msg == 'quit': break
    found = False
    for key, resp in answers.items():
        if key in msg:
            print('Bot:', resp); found = True; break
    if not found: print('Bot: Try asking about', list(answers)[:3])

codes.title: Keyword chatbot
codes.description: Expand answers dict or load JSON.

name: Stock Market Simulation
description: Track mock stock prices over two weeks, calculate percentage changes, and analyse portfolio performance.
guide:
What you will build

Spreadsheet portfolio of 5 fictional stocks — daily prices, daily % change, and total portfolio value graph.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Start with 100,000 TZS virtual cash
    Buy 5 stocks in equal amounts day 1.
  2. Record prices daily 10 school days
    Teacher provides or students invent realistic swings.
  3. % change formula
    (new-old)/old × 100 per stock per day.
  4. Portfolio value chart
    Line graph day vs total value.
  5. Write analysis
    Which stock was most volatile? Best investment?

name: Fractal Generation
description: Draw Sierpinski triangle by hand and with Python turtle, exploring self-similar patterns.
guide:
What you will build

Manual Sierpinski triangle to 3 iterations, then Python turtle version to 5 iterations.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Draw equilateral triangle
    Mark midpoints of each side.
  2. Cut middle triangles iteratively
    Three smaller triangles remain; repeat.
  3. Count triangles at each stage
    1, 3, 9, 27 pattern.
  4. Python turtle recursive function
    sierpinski(points, depth) calls itself 3 times.
  5. Screenshot output
    Paste in notebook with iteration explanation.

Code to upload

Sierpinski turtle (Python)

import turtle
def tri(a,b,c,depth):
    if depth==0: turtle.goto(a); turtle.pendown(); return
    # find midpoints, call tri on three sub-triangles

name: Pendulum Period Investigation
description: Measure how pendulum length affects period and verify T relates to square root of length.
guide:
What you will build

Five pendulums of different string lengths — time 10 oscillations each and graph length vs period.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build stand and bob
    Same mass all tests; only length changes.
  2. Lengths 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 cm
    Release from small angle (<15°).
  3. Time 10 full swings
    Period = total time ÷ 10.
  4. Plot graph
    Length (x) vs period (y).
  5. Compare to T = 2π√(L/g)
    Discuss if pattern matches physics formula.

name: School Layout Optimization
description: Map school buildings as a graph and find shortest routes between classrooms using path counting.
guide:
What you will build

A scale map where nodes are buildings and edges are paths — you find minimum-distance routes from gate to library, lab, and hall.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Walk and measure paths
    Tape distances between key buildings.
  2. Draw graph diagram
    Nodes labelled, edges weighted in metres.
  3. Find shortest path by inspection
    Try different routes; sum weights.
  4. Timed walk test
    Compare two routes gate→lab — faster matches shorter?
  5. Propose one improvement
    New path or sign that saves student time.

equipment.name: School map or permission to measure

name: Optimization Problems Challenge
description: Solve packaging and budget problems using graphs of inequalities to maximise profit or minimise cost.
guide:
What you will build

Worked solutions to two word problems: farmer crop mix and factory box dimensions — with shaded feasible regions.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Problem 1: define variables
    x acres crop A, y acres crop B.
  2. Write constraint inequalities
    Land, water, labour limits.
  3. Plot on graph paper
    Shade feasible region.
  4. Test corner points
    Evaluate profit at each corner.
  5. Problem 2: minimise material
    Repeat method; write optimal solution sentence.

name: Compound Interest Investment Simulator
description: Build a spreadsheet comparing simple and compound interest on a savings account over 10 years.
guide:
What you will build

Excel/Sheets model: 50,000 TZS at 8% annual — columns for simple interest vs compound balance year 0–10.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Simple interest column
    Balance = P + P×r×t each year.
  2. Compound column
    Balance = previous × (1 + r).
  3. Graph both lines
    Year vs balance — compound curves upward.
  4. Calculate difference at year 10
    How much extra from compounding?
  5. Real-life reflection
    Why banks advertise compound savings.

name: Design a Playground
description: Design a playground for your school: measure space, calculate areas, budget materials, and build a scale model.
guide:
What you will build

Scale drawing 1:100 plus cardboard model with swing zone, football area, and path — areas labelled in m².

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Measure available plot
    Length × width with permission.
  2. Allocate zones on graph paper
    Play equipment, open field, seating.
  3. Calculate each zone area
    Rectangle and triangle formulas.
  4. Estimate material budget
    Gravel path cost per m² from teacher price list.
  5. Build cardboard model
    Labels and scale bar 1:100.
  6. Present to class
    One minute pitch why design is safe and fun.

name: Plan a Trip Budget Project
description: Plan a class trip to a nearby city: transport, food, lodging costs, distances, and total per student.
guide:
What you will build

Complete trip budget spreadsheet for 30 students visiting a city 200 km away — itemised costs and per-student share.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Choose destination and research costs
    Bus hire, meals, museum entry (realistic estimates).
  2. Calculate transport
    km × fuel/bus quote ÷ 30 students.
  3. Add food and activities
    Per person × 30.
  4. Contingency 10%
    Add to total.
  5. Per-student total
    Present table and one cost-saving idea.

name: Symmetry in Architecture Hunt
description: Photograph local buildings showing reflection or rotational symmetry and classify each example.
guide:
What you will build

Poster with 6 building photos labelled: line symmetry, rotational symmetry, or both — with sketch lines drawn on prints.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Walk school/neighbourhood
    Photograph facades, windows, gates.
  2. Draw symmetry lines on prints
    Mirror line for reflection.
  3. Identify rotational order
    e.g. square window — 90° rotation match.
  4. Sort into table
    Building name | symmetry type | sketch.
  5. Write why architects use symmetry
    Balance, beauty, structure — 3 sentences.

name: Water Tank Volume Problem
description: Build scale models of tanks in different shapes, calculate volumes, and compare filling rates.
guide:
What you will build

Cardboard cylinder and rectangular prism tanks — measure dimensions, calculate volume, fill with water and time fill rate.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Build two tank models
    Seal seams with tape for water test.
  2. Measure internal dimensions in cm
    radius and height for cylinder; l×w×h for prism.
  3. Calculate volume cm³ then litres
    ÷ 1000 for litres.
  4. Time fill from cup
    Constant pour rate — compare predicted vs actual fill time.
  5. Which shape holds more for same floor area?
    Short report conclusion.

name: Arduino Line-Following Car
description: Build an Arduino car that follows a black line track using two or three IR sensors under the chassis.
guide:
What you will build

Complete car form-factor line follower (not just breadboard) — follows tape loop on floor.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Mount 2 IR sensors front underside
    Spacing matches tape width (~2 cm).
  2. Assemble car with L298N
    Same motor wiring as line-following robot project.
  3. Calibrate on white vs black
    Serial print sensor values.
  4. PID optional extension
    Start with if/else left/right/forward logic.
  5. Lap timer

name: Building Model Satellite
description: Design and build a scale model satellite with solar panels and antenna, explaining each subsystem role.
guide:
What you will build

Cardboard and foil model showing bus body, solar wings, dish antenna, and labelled science payload bay.

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Research satellite diagram
    Label: power, communication, propulsion, instruments.
  2. Build central bus
    Shoebox size scale model.
  3. Add foil solar panels on straws
    Foldable hinge optional.
  4. Antenna from foil dish or wire
    Point toward “Earth” side marked.
  5. Present subsystem poster
    What each part does in orbit.
